data.narrative:
Signaloid is a Seed-stage semiconductor company that has raised $10M to date. The valuation analysis leverages a comp universe of 3 public semiconductors (ALAB, NVDA, AMD) and 8 private peers in Chips & Semiconductors, including Series A companies SambaNova Systems ($11.0B), Rebellions ($2.3B), and d-Matrix ($2.0B).

Two valuation methods are applicable. Stage-progression analysis applies a 2.5x step-up multiplier typical of Seed-to-next-stage advancement, yielding $25M. Peer-median triangulation across the 3 same-sector, same/adjacent-stage comparables produces $2.3B, with a peer range of $2.0B to $11.0B. Public-comp anchoring via P/S multiples (sector median 18.4x) cannot be applied absent the target's revenue disclosures, typical for private companies.

The two-method triangulation supports a valuation range of $21M (low) to $2.7B (high), with a median of $1.2B. This wide dispersion reflects material uncertainty: the stage-progression method implies minimal mark-up from capital raised, while peer-median anchoring to Series A valuations assumes comparable progress. Key uncertainties include the target's revenue trajectory, technical differentiation relative to named peers, and whether near-term fundraising will occur at Seed or Series A terms. The median of $1.2B assumes convergence toward peer-stage multiples but should be stress-tested against product-market fit evidence and competitive positioning within the chip design frontier-tech segment.
